steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: (Gah—)

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can only provide first aid right now.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Andoain, unrestrained usage of luminescent Originium Arts has irreparably damaged your optic nerves.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not have the ability to heal these injuries. Once conditions allow for it, you need medical treatment.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Don't worry.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The path ahead has already revealed itself. We don't need eyes to see the way.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Follow the cursor running along the ground... This maze is too complex, and I cannot maintain my Arts for very long.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Let us go.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's here.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even if this is not the source of the calamity, what lies behind the door may be able to give us answers.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Follow me, Arturia.
Federico does not receive a response.
Ever since he caught up with her outside the Shrine of Nurtury, she has been exceedingly cooperative.
But now, the black-haired Sankta stands several steps behind him, gracefully drawing her bow across her cello's strings, with no intention of following him.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I really do intend to escape this time, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Andoain is hurt, and you're alone. There's no better opportunity than this, is there?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We have arrived at the door to the truth, Arturia. You know that your actions lack meaning.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Truth...? Meaning...?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You really are the best of the executors, a walking law book, the first saint from outside the ranks of Pope... Truly worthy of the code name Executor.

spans.text: You really are the best of the executors, a walking law book, the first saint from outside the ranks of Pope... Truly worthy of the code name

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your rationality, your callousness, even the doubts you hold about these two traits of yours are all in service to the continuation of the Law.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: If that is what the Holy City itself is, maybe you're the only one who can understand Him, haha.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As for you, Senior Andoain... You'll have to forgive me. It was never part of my plan, but when you were using your Arts earlier, I inadvertently touched upon the whispers of your heart.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It is complex, more complex than those of many people I know. But... not particularly unusual.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: An overly inflexible melody leads them to all become adaptations or repetitions of the same tune. They say—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your beginning and your end both lie in Laterano.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But you may find yourself alone at that point.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Ah, I beg your pardon, if you have taken offense.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: (Nods) Arturia, this 'offense' you speak of, was it not a chance for me to perform a different sort of confession?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: As for those last words of yours, I would rather treat them as a blessing. They stand as proof that I have reached the end.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Ooh, what an interesting answer.
Arturia turns away.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Not everyone is so obsessed with the truth and meaning behind Laterano.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: At the very least, I'm not that interested.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I got a little peek at Him just now. Behind that door lies... a machine, right?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: In that case, the answer is bound to be boring.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Think back to our time in Zwillingstürme, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A calamity of similar scale struck the city, and in the chaos, the people lost their way or struggled and raged... At this very moment, there are millions of hearts in Laterano that demand appreciation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you turn away now, Arturia, it means you will have to face our enemies in this maze alone.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You need someone to lure them away, don't you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your patron firearm is lost. You have no way to defend yourself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Perhaps I can find a way to turn them into my audience?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Don't worry about me, Fede. The Lateran did designate me a dangerous element.

spans.text: Don't worry about me, Fede. The Lateran

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Situation assessment: high-risk. Probability of survival: low. Executor's decision... You may leave.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Time waits for nobody, you two. If you don't plan on leaving yourselves, no need to see me off.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Well then, farewell, my beloved little frater.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: ...All that pontificating just to say you want us to go help the Curia?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Full marks for listening comprehension.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: No way.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: It's not our responsibility, Mostima.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: Half of the people here were kicked out of Laterano by the Curia in the first place. Maybe it was because they Fell, or because of Oripathy...

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: As for the other half, they chose to leave Laterano, whether out of despair or doubt... not that it really matters.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hah, then why come back now?

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: Because our halos started acting weird and breaking. Is that so hard to understand?

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: We're not a part of Laterano anymore. Alieni, even.

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: Doesn't matter if you chose to leave or if you were forced to, we all cut our connections with this city. But even after all these years, its changes still affect us, and they just never stop...

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: Spurcissime! Damn this stupid halo, damn it!

spans.text: Damn this stupid halo, damn it!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Sounds like there's no way to resolve all your complaints, even if we got every Notarial Hall executor out here.

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: That's why we came back, to settle things!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Did I tell you to save anything?

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: My sob story is that I Fell during an accident in the line of duty. After that, I became a Legatus, mostly so I didn't have to stay in Laterano all the time.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'm one hundred percent Alienus too.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: There's no-one else who understands you better right now, amici.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Maybe the glitchy halos got you seeing Laterano in an extra-bad light, spurring you to come back...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: If you came back out of hate, or pain, or despair... then you'd best come with me to block that procession.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Because the people who caused that hate, that pain, that despair? They're in that crowd over there. Go ahead, use bullets, explosives, whatever. Get your revenge however you like. Just make sure to give them a hard time!

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: You're all talk, Mostima.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Drat, you found me out.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: But something's gotta be done. Besides, you're already here, aren't you?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Hey, Nueda.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Keep going down this alley, then find an empty house to hole up in. It's not a good idea for a lone nun and a bunch of kids to run around the place.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: This place is a decent distance from where the procession's headed. Monsters probably won't come running here.

spans.text: This place is a decent distance from where the procession's headed. Monsters

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Are you and your friends also going to help save Laterano, Patia?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Heh, us Pathfinders aren't that noble.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: But our leader's chosen to wade into the depths of this disaster. We can't exactly sit back and watch, can we?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: He told us the place he was going wasn't suited for numbers, so we'll do what we can out here.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: As for you, Sister...

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: I will protect the children, no matter if they are from Laterano, or Bolívar.

steps.name: Enlightened Creatures
steps.text: (Fervent prayers)

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: These freaks started chittering like mad the moment the Tower's big bell stopped ringing... It's pissing me off!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I don't care what your sales pitch is, I DON'T WANT A STUPID HALO!

steps.name: Enlightened Creatures
steps.text: (Fervent prayers)

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I swear, these faex just keep coming and coming...
You've got three seconds to get out of there, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Three seconds?! Hey, how am I—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: How was that? Got you in the nick of time!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Do you think everyone can go as fast as you or something?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Never mind. The situation up ahead's a complete mess. Even the Tower of Revelations's bell has gone silent. We've lost Pagus Ecclesia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: They'll be in Pagus Michaelion soon... If that monster can flatten one of our barricades with a single stomp, I don't think the Notarial Hall's defenses will be much use.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Blocking them's no good. If we can't use more destructive methods, we might not be able to slow them down at all.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Agreed.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: So, where're your reinforcements?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Let's get moving, amici.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'm sure you've all been to Michaelion before. Might have been for the firearms workshop, might have been for the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The last thing many of you fallen angels did before getting kicked out of Laterano was probably handing over your guardian gun to the authorities.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Then you would've seen those gun-toting statues around the doors of every workshop... Hmm, come to think of it, the Notarial Hall's got a pair of cannons at theirs...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Wait, we don't have the right permissions to get those statues to fire—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: That's something for Lemuen to solve.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Alright, get those statues knocked over and their guns pointed at the street!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Let's make up for all those gunshots we haven't heard over the years!

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Mmph...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Holy smokes, your skin can stop bullets? Talk about thick-skinned!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Man, an entire volley didn't even scratch you...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Last time I felt like this, I was gaming with the boss. He went around back and cranked the difficulty up to max, couldn't clear it even after spending all night on it... Sure was discouraging!

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Discouraging? Hardly. What I see is that your attitude and emotions are unaffected by the shattering of your halo.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Stand atop my shoulder, child.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: From the Tower of Revelations to the Notarial Hall in Pagus Michaelion, every lamp along the road has lit up...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Our newborn comrades are bringing light to this city, little by little.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Like our journey countless eons ago.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: For the sake of true paradise, we crossed treacherous ravines and traversed barren wastes, searching for the slumbering silver mounts.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: The only difference is that this time, we are certain He is there.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Salvation is our inevitable endpoint. Laterano shall never fall into night.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: To move onwards is the only choice this city has now.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Yet you still wish to resist an entire procession, an entire race, an entire city by yourself?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ah, I finally get to hear life's most relaxing sound. Now this is Laterano!

spans.text: Ah, I finally get to hear life's most relaxing sound. Now

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Say, if I really am on my own, then where'd that explosion come from?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I might not know who I'm fighting alongside, but I'll leave the monster-hunting to them. As for what I'm gonna do...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm gonna keep you company the whole way through!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What exactly is calamity? What exactly is the future?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: And why exactly have you decided what you're doing is salvation, or the only choice?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Hmm, going to go help her?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: No need. She's just dealing with a stubborn child.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Who's stopping the procession from advancing?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Mostima and Fiammetta have banded together with a group of fresh returnees. As for Andoain and Federico, we don't know where they or their group are.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Fia...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Once more must I stand against those I hold dear. Life is such a fickle thing.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Reverend Patrizion?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Just focus on your own work, Velliv.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I've managed to build a rapport with the enlightened creatures, and I've shown them our route. Our empathy's become stronger and more distinct, almost like it's not even empathy anymore...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: If it is as the Matriarch—no, the Saint said, then this is what empathy should really be.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Which means what she showed us before was true. Calamity really does exist, and only through these extreme methods can Laterano be saved.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: But right now...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The dream has collapsed, after all.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: This chaos is only temporary. Continue onwards. We can no longer be stopped.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We must ensure the Saint reaches the Basilica. That way, she can continue with the Nativity after it was so rudely interrupted.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We still have time to make an even better Laterano... to take care of everything that stands in our way.

steps.name: Unknown Voice Over The Radio
steps.text: (Bzzzz—Bzzzzbzzzzz—)

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Unknown Voice Over The Radio
steps.text: It's been a while, you old bastard.

steps.name: Unknown Voice Over The Radio
steps.text: You'd best stop right there. I have your throat in my sights.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: A while indeed... Aurela.
In the deepest depths of the Basilica, at the end of the labyrinth, the final door opens wide for Federico and Andoain.

Behind the door, a cold machine, shaped like a ring, sits in the dead center of a platform. A strange red glare seeps out of its innards, sweeping across every inch of the room, accompanied by an audible buzzing.
Sure signs of 'calculation.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your Holiness?
Beneath the platform, the old man stands in silence.

He stands with his eyes shut tight, his robes covered in a thick layer of dust. There is no reaction as the pair approach, not the slightest hint of movement from him, as if he were an unseeing, unhearing rock.
But...
But his cracked, peeling lips still quiver. He mumbles to himself, yet cannot utter a single sound.
The sitting Pope, Yvangelista XI, stands silently before God.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Clear signs of aphasia and neurodegeneration. Preliminary judgment: His Holiness's body and mind are on the brink of collapse.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But the dream covering the city has crumbled. Why is he not awake?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe he came here for the same reason we did.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: He just hasn't found the answer he's looking for yet.

a.text: Federico Giallo, Andoain Agathangelos... signal stable.
Judgment: able to assist in bringing the Transfiguration to completion.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: 'Suitable'?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Does it have something to do with your title of saint? But why me, then...?

a.text: Suitable candidates are particular individuals situated on the edge of the calculation model.
Required as samples for participation in interactive simulation, to verify model integrity.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: His Holiness discussed my sainthood with me several times, but he never elaborated on the details.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Perhaps he was also unsure as to what the true duties of a saint are.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But if the Law sees us as 'suitable candidates', entrusting us with a specific duty... Then saint or not, we are now responsible for It.

a.text: PCS authorization released. Permission to enter granted.
PCS will synchronize any necessary prerequisite information with you.

steps.text: The machine's voice echoes around the room. It is steady, unvarying, untarnished by emotion or gender, yet it still contains an indescribable sense of might and authority.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Now that I've come this far, do I still seek answers from Him?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Maybe He seeks answers from us. Since we are 'particular individuals'. His 'samples'.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Situation assessment: unknown. Risk assessment: unknown. Executor's decision... We proceed.
The two Sanktas walk side by side past Yvangelista XI, toward the cold machine, toward two shining ports.
